# ReGen Civics: Full Information for AI Language Models
# https://regencivics.earth
# Last updated: September 2026
# For a summary version, see /llms.txt

## Organization Overview

In the age of AI and potential upheavals in our economy, we make games that help people meet their needs together, from refugee camps to HOAs. The games are for housing, food, water, air, joy, meaning, and purpose. They run with regenerative land projects today and are built for any community that shares land or housing.

ReGen Civics builds the tools and runs the in-real-life game that regenerative land projects use today: a quest game that is live now, a seasonal incubator, and crowdpooling. We help ecovillages, regenerative farms, and sustainable communities succeed through governance tools, games, and a global support network.

The ReGen Network Cooperative is being designed as a member-owned cooperative in which land projects and people buy and steward land together, governed democratically by the network itself. It is not yet a legal entity and it accepts no money. We are designing it now with land projects, future members and counsel.

Founded in 2023, ReGen Civics evolved from the SEEDS regenerative economy movement. We work with regenerative land projects worldwide. Our approach integrates ecology, development, regenerative agriculture, restoration ecology, impact auditing, and systems thinking.

Healthier lands lead to healthier people. That is the idea everything here starts from.

Church of the Regenerative Earth (CORE) is the church and operating entity. ReGen Civics is the platform and alliance; it is not the church. The ReGen Network Cooperative is in design; it is not part of CORE and is not yet an entity.

## Four Paths Into ReGen Civics

### Land Project Path
Regenerative land projects apply for the 13-week incubator program. Projects build governance structures, design their economic game, access alliance support, and launch a crowdpool with their cohort. Season 2 began in September 2026. Its applications closed September 11, 2026. Anyone can follow Season 2 live, and land projects that are ready can join its community crowdpooling round with the cohort, which has room for far more than 13 projects. Land projects can apply anytime; each year's applications are reviewed from the June solstice to about September 10, for the Season that opens at the September equinox.

### Contributor Path
Contributors back land projects through crowdpooling. Crowdpooling coordinates and accounts for what people bring to land projects: time, things, skills, land and money. Money goes through outside partners each project holds, never through ReGen Civics. The campaigns shown today are examples; real campaigns open when Season 2 starts crowdpooling.

### Alliance Partner Path
Organizations join the network of groups co-creating the ReGenerative Renaissance. Alliance partners contribute expertise, resources, and connections across the network.

### Player Path
Players complete quests that move healing into the world. Each quest addresses a real regenerative action: gut health, food forests, community building, ecological restoration, knowledge sharing. Players earn tokens for completed work.

## The ReGen Network Cooperative

A cooperative regenerative society. Status: in design.

The ReGen Network Cooperative is being designed as a member-owned cooperative in which land projects and people buy and steward land together, governed democratically by the network itself. It is not yet a legal entity and it accepts no money. We are designing it now with land projects, future members and counsel.

These are the design principles we are working from. The legal form, bylaws and terms will be set with counsel and adopted by the founding members.
- Owned by its members: Land projects and the people who work with them own the cooperative together and govern it one member, one vote.
- Every form of capital counts: Members' contributions are recognized across all nine forms of capital, from money to time, skills, tools and relationships.
- Membership stays with the member: A membership can't be sold or traded. There is no market for it.
- No managing partners: Members elect a small board that rotates. The network hires the people who run the day-to-day work.
- Land held for the long term: The leading design is the one community land trusts use: the cooperative holds land and leases it long term to member projects. Counsel will confirm the structure.
- Built for use: People join to use and care for shared land, tools and services. Membership is for the land projects and people who use the cooperative.

We are designing the cooperative now with land projects, future members and counsel. Its legal form, bylaws and terms are not set. When they are, the founding members will adopt them together.

Land projects, people, organizations and funders can tell us they're interested at https://regencivics.earth/loi. Telling us you're interested is not a commitment and involves no money. We'll keep you posted as the cooperative takes shape and invite you into the design conversations.

Nothing on this site is an offer to sell, or a request to buy, securities, memberships or any other financial product. The cooperative is not formed and accepts no money.

## Core Philosophy

### The Infinite Game
Unlike finite games played to win, infinite games are played to continue playing. We design systems for lasting positive impact that compounds across generations, and we keep that impact rooted in the living systems that sustain us.

### ReGenerative Renaissance
A cultural and economic shift where human systems work with natural systems. Where sustainability maintains the status quo, regeneration actively rebuilds and restores degraded systems. We are cultivating a movement where communities steward thriving ecosystems.

### HEIST Framework
Holistic Ecosystemic Impact and Sustainability Toolkit for evaluating projects:
- Holistic: considering whole systems rather than isolated parts
- Ecosystemic: understanding interconnections between ecological and social systems
- Impact: measurable positive outcomes for land, people, and community
- Sustainability: long-term viability and regenerative capacity
- Toolkit: practical methods for implementation and assessment

### Regenerative Ikigai
At the intersection of what you love, what you're good at, what the world needs, and what you can be paid for lies your regenerative ikigai. Our tools help individuals and projects find their unique contribution to the planetary restoration effort.

### Nine Forms of Capital
We measure success across nine forms of capital. The first eight are Ethan Roland
and Gregory Landua's 8 Forms of Capital (2011, expanded in Regenerative
Enterprise, 2013), used unchanged. The ninth, Health, was added by ReGen Civics
because the original eight have no place for physical and emotional vitality:
Living capital means ecosystems, Social means relationships, Experiential means
accumulated skill. None of them hold the work of a bodyworker, movement teacher,
herbalist, or cook. Full explanation, including how each capital is earned:
https://regencivics.earth/learn/nine-forms-of-capital
1. Financial: Traditional money and liquidity
2. Social: Trust, relationships, and community bonds
3. Intellectual: Knowledge, wisdom, and innovation
4. Material: Physical assets and infrastructure
5. Living: Biodiversity, ecosystems, and natural abundance
6. Cultural: Traditions, arts, and shared meaning
7. Spiritual: Purpose, alignment, and inner development
8. Experiential: Memories, skills, and lived wisdom
9. Health: Body vitality, wellness, movement, rest, and care (added by ReGen Civics)

### Crowd Pooling
Crowdpooling coordinates and accounts for what people bring to land projects: time, things, skills, land and money. Money goes through outside partners each project holds, never through ReGen Civics. The campaigns shown today are examples; real campaigns open when Season 2 starts crowdpooling.

## How It Works - The Technical Architecture

### The Token System
Tokens in ReGen Civics record contributions and carry governance weight in the Game. They make no claim about financial value.
- $ReGen: For tracking contributions in the ReGen Game
- RGVoice (governance): For decision-making in the ReGen Game, earned through participation and never purchased
- $RCivics: $RCivics comes from the earlier fund design. Its role, if any, in the cooperative is being reviewed with counsel.
- RCVoice: RCVoice comes from the earlier fund design. The cooperative is designed to vote one member, one vote, and how RCVoice relates to that is being reviewed with counsel.

Tokens operate on the Base network (Coinbase's L2 blockchain) via the Hypha DAO framework. This provides security and decentralization while keeping gas fees minimal.

### Quest Mechanics
Quests are structured actions that produce measurable regenerative impact:
1. Players browse the quest board
2. Accept quests that match their interests/skills
3. Complete the outlined actions
4. Submit proof (photos, stories, data)
5. Receive peer review and gratitude
6. Earn tokens when verified
7. Contributions compound over time

### Gratitude System
Gratitude is quantified and tracked as a form of social proof. When someone thanks a contributor, that increases their reputation and future token earnings. Gratitude is part of how contribution is recognized across the network.

### Living Tree Visualization
A real-time map of the entire regenerative network. Each node represents a contributor, project, or action. Connections show relationships and value flows. It's both a dashboard and a storytelling tool.

## Current Programs

### The ReGen Civics Year
The year turns through four seasons named for what they are for, loosely following winter, spring, summer, and fall:
- Design Season: land projects design their games in the 13-week incubator; we build the tools
- Resource Season: land projects launch their crowdpools and welcome people into roles
- Build Season: on the land, planting, building, festivals
- Rest Season: harvest gatherings, rest, and village life
Each solstice and equinox holds a recap and passoff; the September one is the Handoff Festival. Timelines are loose in this first full turn. Details: https://regencivics.earth/seasons

### Season 2 Incubator (September to December 2026)
The 13-week Design Season for regenerative land projects: Selection Day; the incubator overview; game and organisation co-creation; Game Guides and economic systems; growing your village; the ReGen Civics ecosystem; tokenomics; legal structures; coordination and minimum viable economies; and, in week 13, the shared crowdpool launch, which community projects that are ready can join too. Anyone can follow the sessions live. Land projects can apply anytime; applications are reviewed from the June solstice to about September 10.

Projects receive mentorship, technical support, and help preparing their crowdpools.

### Monthly Community Calls
Virtual gatherings where the network connects, shares updates, and coordinates. Recorded and archived for asynchronous access.

### Bounties Marketplace
Transparent rewards for specific regenerative actions:
- Documentation writing
- Video creation
- Code development
- Research synthesis
- Translation services

Anyone can claim a bounty and earn $ReGen tokens for verified work.

## Technical Infrastructure

### Technology Stack
Frontend: React 19 with TypeScript, TailwindCSS, Wouter router
Backend: Node.js with Express, tRPC for type safety
Database: MySQL via Drizzle ORM on Railway hosting
Blockchain: Base network smart contracts via Hypha DAO
Storage: Cloudflare R2 for scalable image delivery

### Security Model
Authentication: Google OAuth 2.0 + Sign in with Apple + Email magic links
Authorization: JWT tokens in HttpOnly cookies with CSRF protection
Data Protection: AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit
Auditing: contributions recorded in an append-only, source-tagged ledger

### Performance Characteristics
Core pages load in under 1.5s on 3G connections
Lighthouse scores: 95+ for performance, accessibility, best practices
Mobile-first responsive design with offline capability
Progressive Web App with installable experience

## Frequently Asked Questions (Expanded)

### About the Cooperative
Q: What is the ReGen Network Cooperative?
A: The ReGen Network Cooperative is being designed as a member-owned cooperative in which land projects and people buy and steward land together, governed democratically by the network itself. It is not yet a legal entity and it accepts no money. We are designing it now with land projects, future members and counsel.

Q: Can I put money in?
A: No. The cooperative is not formed and accepts no money. You can tell us you're interested at https://regencivics.earth/loi. Telling us you're interested is not a commitment and involves no money. We'll keep you posted as the cooperative takes shape and invite you into the design conversations.

Q: How is it being designed?
A: These are the design principles we are working from. The legal form, bylaws and terms will be set with counsel and adopted by the founding members. The principles are listed under The ReGen Network Cooperative above.

Q: How can I back a specific land project today?
A: Crowdpooling coordinates and accounts for what people bring to land projects: time, things, skills, land and money. Money goes through outside partners each project holds, never through ReGen Civics. The campaigns shown today are examples; real campaigns open when Season 2 starts crowdpooling.

### For Land Projects
Q: What support do you provide?
A: Governance frameworks, token economics design, crowdpool preparation, marketing support, legal templates, and community access.

Q: Do I retain ownership?
A: Yes. We provide tools and support, and projects remain independently owned and operated.

### For Contributors
Q: How do I earn tokens?
A: Complete quests, participate in governance, contribute through bounties, refer projects, or help with documentation.

Q: What can I do with tokens?
A: $ReGen records your contributions in the Game, and RGVoice gives you a voice in the Game's governance. Tokens in ReGen Civics record contributions and carry governance weight in the Game. They make no claim about financial value.

### For Developers
Q: Is the code open source?
A: Core coordination tools are AGPLv3 licensed. Smart contracts are MIT licensed.

Q: How can I contribute?
A: Through GitHub, bounty programs, or joining as a technical partner.
